newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech media buying seen at 10.9 bln crowns in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Czech media buying seen at 10.9 bln crowns in 1997.

text.p: Czech media advertising spending totalled 9.95 billion crowns in 1996 and was seen rising to about 10.9 billion in 1997, the Czech unit of French communications group Havas, IP Praha, said on Wednesday.

IP, a media sales representative for Czech public broadcasters, said if the figures included a crown amount given for barter deals, total 1996 spending would have exceeded the previously forecast 10.6 billion, after 9.39 billion in 1995.

IP's Michael Richter told Reuters that press advertising -- thanks to campaigns for two national elections, the start-up of two mobile phone networks, and major sporting events -- led all advertising earnings by taking in 4.3 billion crowns last year.
Television advertising revenue was next with 3.7 billion, while billboard operators received 1.02 billion, radio broadcasters 710 million, and cinemas 220 million, IP said.
Richter said that advertising spending would show the same trend as inflation and the overall development of the economy this year, but would not follow it completely.
He said press advertising would see some stagnation or a relatively smaller growth rate.
"It can be expected that press advertising will stagnate a little bit, because it cannot be expected that there would be massive campaigns like the elections," Richter said.
"This year will be a little poorer in terms of big sporting events like soccer (European championships) or the Olympic Games, which bring more advertising," he said.

Richter added that television revenues might be lower due to the re-launch of private channel Prima, which could evolve into a competitor for private national Nova TV, possibly pushing rate cards lower.

Nova, controlled by Central European Media Enterprises Ltd, a group founded by U.S. investors and listed in New York, has grabbed roughly two-thirds of the television market since opening in early 1994.
Prima, owned primarily by Czech entities and recast from the struggling channel Premiera at the beginning of this year, covers around 60-70 percent of Czech territory with its signal.

Jiri Mikes of the Association of Advertising Agencies (ARA) said that advertising spending, a phenomenon virtually unknown before the fall of communism in 1989, has reached "around one percent" of gross domestic product.
"From there, it will rise only with the growth of the economy," said Mikes.
Procter & Gamble was the largest advertisier, followed by Unilever Plc and the Czech lottery operator Sazka a.s..
